context: The Help tab will display the user guide to assist users in understanding how to work with the RDD framework through the Web UI and VS Code. This questionnaire clarifies design decisions about the Help tab implementation and user guide content.

questions.question-text: Should the Help tab be placed before or after the existing tabs (Active Prompt, Prompts History, Workdir, Files)?

options.label: Place Help tab at the end (after Files tab)
options.pros: Keeps primary workflow tabs at the front, Help is referenced less frequently during active development
options.cons: Users might not discover the Help tab easily when first using the interface

options.label: Place Help tab at the beginning (before Active Prompt tab)
options.pros: New users see Help first, making it easier to discover documentation and get started
options.cons: Experienced users have to navigate past Help to reach workflow tabs they use frequently

options.label: Place Help tab second to last (between Workdir and Files)
options.pros: Balances discoverability with workflow priority, separates from primary action tabs
options.cons: Less intuitive positioning, no clear logic for placement between Workdir and Files

questions.recommendation-rationale: Placing Help at the end keeps the primary workflow tabs (Active Prompt, Prompts History, Workdir, Files) easily accessible for regular users while still making documentation available. Most users will learn the interface quickly and reference Help only occasionally.

questions.question-text: How should the markdown user guide be rendered in the Help tab?

options.label: Use a JavaScript markdown library (like marked.js or showdown.js) to render markdown client-side
options.pros: Simple implementation, works entirely in the browser, no server-side processing needed, fast rendering
options.cons: Adds external dependency, requires loading additional JavaScript library

options.label: Convert markdown to HTML on the server side when the page loads
options.pros: No client-side dependencies, server has full control over rendering, can pre-process content
options.cons: Requires Python markdown library, more complex server implementation, slower page load

options.label: Display raw markdown in a formatted text area or pre tag
options.pros: No dependencies, simplest implementation, works immediately
options.cons: Poor user experience, no styling, links not clickable, images won't display

questions.recommendation-rationale: Client-side markdown rendering with a library like marked.js provides the best user experience with minimal implementation complexity. It keeps the server simple while providing full markdown support including links, formatting, and proper styling.

questions.question-text: What level of detail should the recreated user guide include about the framework structure?

options.label: High-level overview only - explain workflow steps and UI usage without mentioning .rdd/ or .rdd-instance/ internals
options.pros: Simplest for users to understand, focuses on what users do rather than how framework works internally, matches prompt requirement to avoid technical details
options.cons: Users won't understand where files are stored or framework organization

options.label: Include brief mentions of .rdd/ and .rdd-instance/ folders when relevant to user actions
options.pros: Gives users context about framework structure, helps users understand file locations when needed, balances simplicity with useful information
options.cons: Slightly more complex than pure workflow description, may confuse some users

options.label: Detailed explanation of all folders, files, and framework components
options.pros: Complete understanding of framework, users know exactly where everything is located
options.cons: Violates prompt requirement to avoid technical details, overwhelming for new users, too complex for a user guide

questions.recommendation-rationale: Brief mentions of folder structure when relevant provides necessary context without overwhelming users. For example, mentioning that requirements are in .rdd-instance/specifications/ helps users understand the framework organization while keeping focus on usage rather than internals.

questions.question-text: Should the user guide include information about CLI commands or focus only on Web UI?

options.label: Web UI only - describe only how to use the web interface
options.pros: Simplest and most focused guide, matches the prompt context (Help tab in UI), easier to maintain
options.cons: Users won't learn about CLI options, incomplete picture of framework capabilities

options.label: Both Web UI and CLI - include sections for both interfaces
options.pros: Complete documentation, users can choose their preferred interface, shows full framework capabilities
options.cons: Longer guide, may be confusing to present two different ways to do the same thing

options.label: Primarily Web UI with CLI mentioned as alternative for advanced users
options.pros: Focuses on main interface while acknowledging CLI exists, good for both beginners and advanced users
options.cons: May not provide enough CLI detail for users who prefer command line

questions.recommendation-rationale: The Help tab is in the Web UI, so the primary focus should be on Web UI usage. Mentioning CLI as an alternative for advanced users provides complete information while keeping the guide focused and approachable for the main audience.

questions.question-text: Should the user guide include step-by-step workflow examples or just describe features?

options.label: Feature descriptions only - explain what each UI section does
options.pros: Shorter guide, users can figure out their own workflow, easier to maintain
options.cons: Users may not understand how features connect to form a complete workflow

options.label: Include a complete workflow example from start to finish
options.pros: Users see exactly how to use RDD for real development, easier to understand the complete process, matches prompt requirement to be 'logical and simple to follow'
options.cons: Longer guide, specific example may not match all use cases

options.label: Multiple short workflow examples for different scenarios
options.pros: Covers various use cases, flexible for different user needs
options.cons: Significantly longer guide, may be overwhelming, harder to maintain

questions.recommendation-rationale: A single complete workflow example helps users understand how all the pieces fit together. This makes the guide 'logical and simple to follow' as required by the prompt. Users can adapt the example workflow to their specific needs once they understand the overall process.
